'''Esteban Damián Batista Hernández''' (born September 2, 1983) is a Uruguayan former professional [[basketball]] player. He was the first ever Uruguayan to play in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].

==Professional career==
Batista began his pro career in the [[Liga Uruguaya de Basketball|Uruguayan League]] in 2001. He then moved to the second division of Spain, the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|Spanish LEB League]] in 2003.

===NBA===
Batista was signed as a free agent by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on September 12, 2005. He made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut on November 2 of that year, going scoreless in 6 minutes of play time against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. In his first NBA season, Batista averaged 1.8 points per game  and 2.5 rebounds per game in 8.7 minutes per game, in 57 games played.

On September 26, 2007, Batista signed a non-guaranteed contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>Peter May, [https://web.archive.org/web/20110523072015/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2007/09/camp_roster_set.html Camp Roster Set], ''The Boston Globe''.</ref> On October 16, 2007, however, Batista was waived by the team.<ref>Marc Spears, [https://web.archive.org/web/20110523072023/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2007/10/batista_waived.html Batista Waived], ''The Boston Globe''.</ref>

===Europe and China===
On the same day that he was released by the [[Boston Celtics|Celtics]], he signed with the [[EuroLeague]] team [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/16155/180/item Maccabi signs center Esteban Batista] October 22, 2007.</ref>

Batista joined the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Super League]] team [[BC Triumph Lyubertsy|Triumph Lyubertsy]] in December 2008,<ref>[http://www.talkbasket.net/3481-esteban-batista-is-the-new-triumph-center.html Esteban Batista is the new Triumph center]</ref> but left the club shortly thereafter for personal reasons.

Batista signed a three-year contract with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Alta Gestión Fuenlabrada]] at the summer of 2009.<ref name="Conoce">{{cite web|url=http://www.baloncestofuenlabrada.com/?se=noticia&n=579 |title=Conoce a Esteban Batista |publisher=Baloncestofuenlabrada.com |access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> In January 2011, he signed with the [[Euroleague]] team [[Saski Baskonia|Caja Laboral]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/81026/caja-laboral-bulks-up-with-batista-at-center |title=Caja Laboral bulks up with Batista at center |publisher=Euroleague.net |access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref>

In July 2011, he signed a two-year contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/86751/180/anadolu-efes-also-lands-batista |title=Anadolu Efes also lands Batista |publisher=Euroleague.net |access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> In August 2013, he signed a one-year contract with [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] also of the Turkish Basketball League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/105377/esteban-batista-moves-to-pinar-karsiyaka.html |title=Batista moves to Pınar Karşıyaka |publisher=Sportando.net |access-date=August 28, 2013}}</ref>

On July 18, 2014, he signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Panathinaikos lands Esteban Batista|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=26081&lang=2|access-date=18 July 2014|work=paobc.gr}}</ref> On April 5, 2015, he won the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]].

In June 2015, he signed with [[Beikong Fly Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/166157/esteban-batista-signing-in-china.html Esteban Batista signing in China]</ref> On February 6, 2016, after the end of the Chinese season, he signed a deal with [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]] until June 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/190202/olimpia-milano-made-official-the-signing-of-esteban-batista.html |title=Olimpia Milano made official the signing of Esteban Batista |access-date=2016-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820053218/http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/190202/olimpia-milano-made-official-the-signing-of-esteban-batista.html |archive-date=2016-08-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, at the end of the 2015–16 season, he parted ways with Milano.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/204875/olimpia-milano-esteban-batista-expected-to-part-ways.html Olimpia Milano, Esteban Batista expected to part ways]</ref><ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/205735/macvan-cerella-lafayette-to-leave-olimpia-milano.html Macvan, Cerella, Lafayette to leave Olimpia Milano]</ref>

In July 2016, Batista re-signed with Beikong Fly Dragons for the [[2016–17 CBA season]].<ref>[http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/454525/Batista-is-back-at-North-Control Batista is back at North Control]</ref> On February 19, 2017, he signed with Italian club [[Reyer Venezia Mestre]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 Lega Basket Serie A|2016–17 Serie A season]].<ref>[http://www.reyer.it/ufficiale-lumana-reyer-ingaggia-esteban-batista/ Ufficiale: l’Umana Reyer ingaggia Esteban Batista] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728172636/http://www.reyer.it/ufficiale-lumana-reyer-ingaggia-esteban-batista/ |date=2017-07-28 }} {{in lang|it}}</ref>

===Return to Uruguay===
In August 2017, Batista returned to Uruguay and signed with [[Club Atlético Welcome]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/245068/welcome-signs-esteban-batista.html Welcome signs Esteban Batista]</ref>

==National team career==
During his career, Batista was a member of the [[Uruguay national basketball team|Uruguayan national basketball team]]. During the [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]], which was held from August 22 through September 2, in [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]], Batista averaged 20.8 points per game and 12.4 rebounds per game.

On 26 February 2023, Batista played his last game for Uruguay and retired after a 20-year career of 116 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-27 |title=Esteban Batista retires from Uruguay's National Team |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/americas-qualifiers/news/esteban-batista-retires-from-uruguay-s-national-team-i-was-happy-defending-my-country-s-jersey |access-date=2023-02-27 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>
